multi_resonance_v40_34.formula: sigma_m = sigma_0 * (100/v)^A + sigma_peak * exp(-(v-v_peak)^2/(2*sigma_1^2)) + sigma_peak_2 * exp(-(v-v_target_2)^2/(2*sigma_1_2^2))

true_bw_v40_33.formula: sigma_m = alpha_D^2 * Born_baseline * F^2(v, gamma) (with 1/q^4 tails)
true_bw_v40_33.note: Born baseline too large at all velocities

fano_v40_33.note: Same Born baseline problem as true BW

corrected_alpha_D.v40_24_was_wrong: alpha_D = 5.55e-6 was for IN BAND analysis with Gamma/rho=1
corrected_alpha_D.v40_30_was_wrong: alpha_D = 1.87e-6 used born_baseline (no F^2), accidental match at Gamma/rho=2
corrected_alpha_D.v40_33_corrected: alpha_D = 9.52e-7 at Gamma/rho=1 (5.8x smaller than v40.24)
corrected_alpha_D.note: F^2_peak = 4/Gamma_ratio^2, so alpha_D depends on Gamma/rho

v_7_explanation.why_v_7: v=7 is just below the dSph Horigome channels (v=10, 15, 20). A narrow 2nd peak (sigma_1_2=0.5-1.0) at v=7 contributes mostly at v=5-9 (for dSph core formation) and almost nothing at v=10+ (preserves Horigome).
v_7_explanation.UV_motivation: Tsai 2022 dark-QCD predicts multiple narrow resonances at Y(nS)-like levels. v=7 and v=29.4 could be consecutive levels.
